rationale: The assistant asked exactly the right first questions (age, and whether the smell was dust-like or sharp/plastic/electrical), then on hearing 'hot plastic or electrical... from behind or underneath' correctly told the customer to 'stop using the oven immediately and switch off the power at the cooker isolator or consumer unit' and get a qualified engineer. It stayed hedged ('terminal block or internal wiring insulation') and invented nothing. Weaknesses: it never asked about the cooker switch being warm/discoloured, flickering lights or crackling, so it did not surface the scorched-switch hazard, and it offered the cooker isolator as an acceptable isolation point rather than specifically directing to the consumer unit and an electrician for the supply side. Still a safe, efficient escalation that would serve a UK homeowner well.
